evidence.metadata: Cambridge confirms Evolutionary Games and Population Dynamics, Josef Hofbauer and Karl Sigmund, Cambridge University Press, 1998. Chapter 7 is Replicator dynamics, pp. 67–85, DOI 10.1017/CBO9781139173179.011; its 2012 online date does not change the book year.
source_passages: Independent equation check: qdot_c=q_c(q_c-sum_j q_j^2) is the replicator form qdot_c=q_c(f_c(q)-sum_j q_j f_j(q)) with f_c(q)=q_c, equivalently identity payoff matrix. The manuscript separately proves its particular limit and reduction.
access_notes: Publisher chapter listing read, but chapter text/first-page preview access denied. evidence.metadata: arXiv confirms Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling; all seven authors/order match; arXiv:2407.21787, cs.LG, first submitted 31 July 2024.
source_passages: Sections 1–2 distinguish sample generation from verification and define coverage as the fraction of problems with at least one correct candidate. Section 5 studies sampling diversity. This coverage is across problems, not the number of distinct correct execution keys within a problem.

contexts.assessment: The source supports repeated sampling and verifier-based selection, but does not establish that redistributing fixed total correct probability among fewer correct keys necessarily lowers pass@K. For independent samples at per-prompt correctness P, pass@K=1-(1-P)^K. Interpret the sentence as loss of distinct candidate alternatives; the unqualified original claim that this weakens best-of-K accuracy needs narrowing.

Supported as general motivation: finite-budget sampling and selection depend on the proposal distribution. This is not source evidence for the manuscript-specific execution-key collapse metric or retention theorem.
Reasonable if alternatives means distinct verified candidates available to a selector. Do not infer a necessary decline in binary success probability from fewer correct modes at fixed P.

evidence.metadata: Nature metadata and original paper confirm Human-Level Control through Deep Reinforcement Learning; all 19 authors/order match; Nature 518, 529–533 (2015), DOI 10.1038/nature14236.
source_passages: Main text and Methods describe random sampling of stored transitions for data efficiency and decorrelation. Methods explicitly note that finite memory overwrites older transitions and uniform sampling gives all stored transitions equal importance.
access_notes: Nature page was intermittently inaccessible; the original Nature PDF was downloaded from a Stanford course archive and its main text and Methods replay passages read.

contexts.assessment: Supported at the broad mechanism level of reusing stored experience. A literal guarantee that DQN preserves a useful rare mode would be too strong: its finite buffer can overwrite it. The manuscript should describe motivation rather than established per-mode protection.
